grants.deadline_text: Rolling — applications reviewed 3x/yr (Mar, Jul, Nov meetings)
grants.notes: Rolling submission and generous terms make this one of Europe's best postdoc routes. Alumni network is exceptional.

grants.title: Humboldt Research Fellowship for Experienced Researchers
grants.description: For researchers with more experience, funding flexible research stays in Germany that can be split into up to three visits.
grants.eligibility: PhD within 12 years; any nationality except German; German host required
grants.notes: Flexible splitting suits researchers who cannot leave their home post for a long block.

grants.title: Georg Forster Research Fellowship
grants.description: Humboldt fellowships reserved for researchers from developing and transition countries working on development-relevant topics.
grants.eligibility: Researchers from eligible developing/transition countries; German host required
grants.notes: Same generous terms as the standard Humboldt with an explicit development focus.

grants.title: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.description: Prestigious two-year fellowships for postdocs in the life sciences moving between countries, with extensive career support.
grants.amount: Competitive salary/stipend + travel and childcare allowances
grants.eligibility: PhD within 2 years at application; international move required; life sciences
grants.notes: Includes lab leadership courses and a strong alumni network. Widely seen as a career marker.

grants.title: EMBO Installation Grants
grants.region: Selected EMBC states (CZ, EE, GR, HR, LT, LU, PL, PT, TR)
grants.description: Helps life scientists establish independent laboratories in participating countries with lower research investment.
grants.eligibility: Establishing a first independent lab in an eligible country; typically 2-9 years post-PhD
grants.notes: An excellent and under-applied route for scientists willing to start a lab outside the usual hubs.

grants.title: Branco Weiss Fellowship — Society in Science
grants.description: Unusually free fellowship: postdocs pursue an independent, unconventional project anywhere in the world, with no obligation to a host institution's agenda.
grants.eligibility: PhD within 5 years; project must depart from mainstream research; any nationality, host anywhere
grants.notes: Perhaps the most intellectually free fellowship in existence — designed for people who do not fit standard schemes.

grants.title: Schmidt Science Fellows
grants.description: Funds a deliberate change of discipline: a postdoc year in a field different from your PhD, plus a global meeting series.
grants.eligibility: Final-year PhD or recent PhD in natural sciences, engineering, maths or computing; university nomination required
grants.notes: Nomination-only: your university's research office selects candidates, so ask early.

grants.title: NWO Veni
grants.description: First step of the Dutch Talent Programme, giving recently graduated researchers three years to develop their own ideas.
grants.eligibility: PhD within 3 years; hosted at a Dutch research institution
grants.notes: Veni-Vidi-Vici is the standard Dutch academic career ladder.

grants.title: NWO Vidi
grants.description: For researchers who have already shown they can generate innovative ideas independently, funding their own research line and group.
grants.eligibility: Typically up to 8 years post-PhD; Dutch host institution
grants.notes: The middle rung: usually taken when moving toward a permanent position.

grants.title: NWO Vici
grants.description: For senior researchers building their own research group, typically alongside a move to a professorship.
grants.eligibility: Typically up to 15 years post-PhD; senior researchers at Dutch institutions
grants.notes: The senior rung of the Dutch talent ladder.

grants.title: Leverhulme Trust Early Career Fellowships
grants.description: Three-year fellowships helping early-career researchers in the UK establish an academic career, with salary matched by the host.
grants.amount: ~50% of salary from Leverhulme + £6,000/yr research expenses
grants.eligibility: PhD submitted within ~5 years; UK host institution which must co-fund
grants.notes: Host institutions run internal selection first — contact potential hosts months ahead.

grants.title: UKRI Future Leaders Fellowships
grants.description: The UK's flagship scheme for researchers and innovators establishing independence, spanning academia and business.
grants.eligibility: Early-career researchers or innovators; UK host organisation (university or company)
grants.notes: Unusually flexible: business-based fellows are explicitly welcome.

grants.title: Volkswagen Foundation Freigeist Fellowships
grants.description: For 'free spirits' pursuing risky research between established fields, with exceptional freedom and generous group funding.
grants.eligibility: PhD within ~5 years; German host institution; project must cross disciplinary boundaries
grants.notes: Explicitly rewards proposals that would fail conventional peer review for being too unconventional.

grants.title: Max Planck International Max Planck Research Schools (IMPRS)
grants.description: Structured, fully funded doctoral programmes run jointly by Max Planck Institutes and partner universities across all fields.
grants.amount: Full PhD contract or stipend (typically €1,600-2,600/month net equivalent)
grants.eligibility: Master's degree (or equivalent); international applicants welcome; English-language programmes
grants.notes: Around 60 schools across physics, biology, chemistry, brain sciences, social sciences and more — check the one matching your field.

grants.title: EMBL International PhD Programme
grants.description: One of Europe's most competitive life-science PhD programmes, spread across six EMBL sites with outstanding facilities.
grants.amount: Full EMBL fellowship (competitive stipend, generous benefits)
grants.eligibility: Bachelor's/Master's qualifying for doctoral study; any nationality
grants.notes: Interview week is all-expenses-paid; no fees and excellent conditions.

grants.title: 'la Caixa' INPhINIT Doctoral Fellowships
grants.description: Doctoral fellowships at accredited Spanish and Portuguese research centres, in incoming and retaining strands.
grants.eligibility: Master's completed; mobility rules apply per strand; excellent academic record
grants.notes: Better paid than most European PhD positions, with strong training and networking.

grants.title: FCT PhD Studentships
grants.funding_body: Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT)
grants.description: Portugal's national doctoral studentship competition, funding PhDs at Portuguese institutions across all scientific areas.
grants.eligibility: Admission to a Portuguese doctoral programme; open to international applicants
grants.notes: One of the larger national PhD competitions in southern Europe.

grants.title: NCN Poland — Preludium, Sonata & Polonez BIS
grants.description: Poland's basic-research funder: Preludium for doctoral candidates, Sonata for early researchers and Polonez BIS for incoming international postdocs.
grants.amount: Preludium up to ~PLN 210k; Sonata ~PLN 1.5M; Polonez BIS ~€4,000/mo package
grants.eligibility: Varies by scheme; Polonez BIS requires international mobility into Poland
grants.deadline_text: Two main rounds/yr: ~15 Mar and ~15 Sep
grants.notes: Polonez BIS is MSCA co-funded and pays well above local norms.

grants.title: Swedish Research Council (Vetenskapsrådet) Grants
grants.description: Sweden's principal research funder, with project grants, international postdoc grants and starting grants across all fields.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at Swedish institutions; international postdoc grant requires a move abroad from Sweden
grants.notes: The international postdoc grant funds Swedish-based researchers going abroad, then returning.

grants.title: Research Council of Norway — FRIPRO / Researcher Project for Young Talents
grants.description: Norway's open, bottom-up scheme, including a dedicated track for young talents building their first research group.
grants.amount: NOK 8-12M typical for young talent projects
grants.eligibility: Researchers at approved Norwegian institutions; 2-7 years post-PhD for the young talent track
grants.notes: Norway funds generously per project; English-language applications are standard.

grants.title: Research Council of Finland — Postdoctoral Researcher & Academy Research Fellow
grants.description: Finland's core career funding: postdoctoral researcher funding for the early years and Academy Research Fellow for establishing independence.
grants.eligibility: PhD within eligibility window; Finnish host institution
grants.application_mode: Online services of the Research Council
grants.notes: Finnish institutions offer strong conditions and English-language working environments.

grants.title: FWO Postdoctoral & PhD Fellowships (Flanders)
grants.description: Flanders' main personal fellowship scheme, with junior and senior tracks for both doctoral and postdoctoral researchers.
grants.eligibility: Hosted at a Flemish university or research institute; nationality-open
grants.deadline_text: Annual: PhD ~1 Mar; postdoc ~1 Dec (check site)
grants.notes: Belgium's French-speaking counterpart is F.R.S.-FNRS with parallel schemes.

grants.title: Novo Nordisk Foundation Research Grants & Fellowships
grants.description: Europe's largest private research funder, with an extensive portfolio from postdoctoral fellowships to major centre grants.
grants.amount: Scheme-dependent (postdoc fellowships ~DKK 2-3M; centre grants far larger)
grants.eligibility: Mostly requires a Danish or Nordic host institution; some international schemes
grants.deadline_text: Scheme-specific deadlines throughout the year (check site)
grants.notes: Grants over DKK 10 billion a year — check the current call list, it changes annually.

grants.title: Lundbeck Foundation Fellowships & Postdoctoral Grants
grants.description: Danish foundation focused on brain research and biomedicine, funding ambitious postdocs and new group leaders.
grants.amount: Fellowships up to DKK 10M; postdoc grants ~DKK 1-3M
grants.eligibility: Danish host institution; career-stage rules per scheme
grants.notes: Especially strong for neuroscience — one of the biggest brain-research funders in Europe.

grants.title: ARC Discovery Early Career Researcher Award (DECRA)
grants.description: Australia's flagship early-career fellowship, funding a salary and project for researchers within five years of their PhD.
grants.eligibility: PhD awarded within 5 years (with career-interruption provisions); Australian host institution
grants.notes: Highly portable and prestigious; medical research goes to NHMRC instead.

grants.title: ARC Future Fellowships
grants.description: Mid-career fellowships designed to attract and retain outstanding researchers in Australia, at 5-15 years post-PhD.
grants.eligibility: 5-15 years post-PhD; Australian host institution; international applicants welcome
grants.notes: Often the bridge to a continuing academic position in Australia.

grants.title: ARC Australian Laureate Fellowships
grants.description: Australia's most prestigious research fellowship, for world-leading researchers building major programmes and mentoring the next generation.
grants.eligibility: Outstanding senior researchers; Australian host institution
grants.notes: Includes dedicated ambassador roles for women in science (Kathleen Fitzpatrick and Georgina Sweet awards).

grants.title: NHMRC Investigator Grants
grants.funding_body: National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC)
grants.description: Australia's consolidated health-research fellowship scheme, funding salary plus a flexible research package at every career level.
grants.eligibility: Health and medical researchers at Australian institutions; levels from Emerging Leader to Leadership
grants.notes: Emerging Leader levels are the entry point for postdocs. Replaced the old fellowship schemes.

grants.title: NHMRC Ideas Grants
grants.funding_body: National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC)
grants.description: Project funding for innovative health and medical research at any career stage, with no requirement for preliminary data.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at Australian administering institutions
grants.notes: The main project-grant vehicle for Australian biomedical researchers.

grants.title: Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) Scholarships
grants.description: The main funding route for research degrees in Australia: fee offsets plus living stipends, allocated by each university.
grants.eligibility: Domestic and international students admitted to an Australian research degree; allocated by the university
grants.notes: You apply to the university, not the government. International places are limited so apply early.

grants.title: CSIRO Early Research Career (CERC) Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.funding_body: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO)
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowships within Australia's national science agency, working on applied problems with industry relevance.
grants.eligibility: PhD within 3 years; any nationality (visa support available)
grants.notes: Advertised like jobs rather than as a single annual call — check the careers page regularly.

grants.title: Marsden Fund
grants.funding_body: Royal Society Te Apārangi / New Zealand Government
grants.description: New Zealand's flagship fund for excellent fundamental research, including a Fast-Start track reserved for early-career researchers.
grants.amount: Standard up to NZD 960k; Fast-Start NZD 360k
grants.eligibility: Researchers at New Zealand institutions; Fast-Start for within 7 years of PhD
grants.notes: Fast-Start is one of the friendliest early-career schemes anywhere — no preliminary data culture.

grants.title: Rutherford Discovery Fellowships
grants.description: Supports outstanding early-to-mid career researchers to build their careers in New Zealand.
grants.eligibility: 3-8 years of research experience post-PhD; New Zealand host institution
grants.notes: Only around ten awarded each year — small but prestigious.

grants.title: Rutherford Foundation Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.description: Postdoctoral fellowships enabling promising early-career researchers to continue research in New Zealand.
grants.eligibility: Recent PhD; New Zealand host institution
grants.notes: Also funds New Zealand doctoral candidates through associated scholarships.

grants.title: Health Research Council of New Zealand — Career Development Awards
grants.funding_body: Health Research Council of New Zealand (HRC)
grants.description: New Zealand's health research funder, with dedicated PhD scholarships, postdoctoral fellowships and clinical research training.
grants.eligibility: Researchers and students at New Zealand institutions; specific tracks for Māori and Pacific health researchers
grants.notes: Includes ring-fenced funding for Māori and Pacific health research careers.

grants.title: JSPS KAKENHI (Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research)
grants.funding_body: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) / MEXT
grants.description: Japan's principal competitive research funding, spanning small early-career grants to large collaborative programmes.
grants.amount: ¥1M to ¥100M+ depending on category (Wakate, Kiban C/B/A, etc.)
grants.eligibility: Researchers affiliated with a Japanese research institution; open to non-Japanese researchers in Japan
grants.deadline_text: Annual: applications ~Sep-Nov for the following fiscal year
grants.notes: The Wakate (Early-Career Scientists) category is the natural entry point after a PhD.

grants.title: JSPS Research Fellowship for Young Scientists (DC1 / DC2)
grants.funding_body: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS)
grants.description: Japan's main doctoral fellowship, paying a monthly stipend plus research funds to outstanding doctoral students.
grants.eligibility: Doctoral students at Japanese universities; DC1 from first year, DC2 later. Some categories restricted to Japanese residents/nationals — check current rules
grants.notes: Highly prestigious in Japan; often decisive for an academic career there.

grants.title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship (PD / SPD / RPD)
grants.funding_body: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS)
grants.description: Domestic postdoctoral fellowships giving new PhDs independence and research funds at a Japanese host institution.
grants.eligibility: PhD holders; specific eligibility per category (RPD supports researchers returning after childbirth/childcare)
grants.notes: Distinct from the JSPS fellowships for overseas researchers — check which category fits you.

grants.title: JST PRESTO (Sakigake)
grants.description: Individual research programme for ambitious young researchers pursuing challenging goals within themed research areas.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at Japanese institutions; typically early to mid career; foreign researchers in Japan eligible
grants.deadline_text: Annual calls by research area (typically ~Mar-May; check site)
grants.notes: Individually held, unusually free by Japanese standards — a strong career marker.

grants.title: JST CREST
grants.description: Team-based research programme funding ambitious goal-oriented basic research in strategic areas.
grants.eligibility: Team leaders at Japanese research institutions
grants.deadline_text: Annual calls by research area (check site)
grants.notes: The team-level counterpart to PRESTO within the same strategic areas.

grants.title: MEXT Scholarship (Japanese Government Scholarship)
grants.funding_body: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
grants.description: Japan's government scholarship for international students, covering research students, master's and doctoral study with full support.
grants.eligibility: International students; apply via Japanese embassy in your country or via a Japanese university recommendation
grants.deadline_text: Embassy route ~Apr-May; university route varies (check site)
grants.notes: Two distinct routes: embassy recommendation (earlier, broader) and university recommendation (needs a host professor).

grants.title: RIKEN Special Postdoctoral Researcher (SPDR) Programme
grants.description: Fellowships at Japan's flagship national research institute, giving postdocs independent research funds and world-class facilities.
grants.eligibility: PhD within 5 years; any nationality; RIKEN host laboratory
grants.notes: Excellent facilities and an international, English-friendly working environment.

grants.title: OIST PhD Program
grants.funding_body: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST)
grants.description: Fully funded, English-language interdisciplinary PhD programme at Japan's international graduate university, with no tuition fees.
grants.amount: ~¥2.4M/yr stipend, no tuition, housing and travel support
grants.eligibility: Bachelor's or Master's degree; any nationality; taught entirely in English
grants.notes: Unusually international for Japan — over half the faculty and most students come from abroad.

grants.title: National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) — Basic Research Programs
grants.description: Korea's principal research funder, covering individual basic research grants from early-career to group and centre level.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at Korean institutions; foreign researchers based in Korea are eligible
grants.notes: Application materials are often Korean-language — plan for local administrative support.

grants.title: Korea Research Fellowship (KRF) / Brain Pool Program
grants.description: Programmes bringing outstanding foreign researchers to Korean institutions: KRF for postdocs, Brain Pool for experienced scientists.
grants.eligibility: Non-Korean researchers with a PhD; Korean host institution required
grants.notes: The main formal route for international researchers to be funded in Korea.

grants.title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) — Graduate Degrees
grants.description: Korea's flagship government scholarship for international students, covering full tuition, living costs and a year of Korean language training.
grants.eligibility: International students; embassy or university track; age and grade requirements apply
grants.deadline_text: Annual: embassy track ~Feb-Mar; university track ~Mar (check site)
grants.notes: Includes a mandatory Korean language year unless waived by proficiency.

grants.title: Institute for Basic Science (IBS) Young Scientist Fellowship
grants.description: Independent research fellowships at Korea's flagship basic-science institute, with substantial autonomy and budget.
grants.eligibility: PhD within ~5 years; any nationality; hosted at an IBS research centre
grants.notes: One of Asia's better-funded early-independence positions, with English as the working language.

grants.title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC)
grants.description: China's principal government scholarship for international students, covering tuition, accommodation and a monthly stipend at Chinese universities.
grants.eligibility: International students; apply via Chinese embassy, university, or partner programme
grants.deadline_text: Annual (typically ~Dec-Apr depending on route; check site)
grants.notes: Several routes (bilateral, university-specific, Silk Road); the university route is usually the most practical.

grants.title: NSFC General Program (面上项目)
grants.funding_body: National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC)
grants.description: China's core competitive research grant for established investigators across the natural sciences.
grants.eligibility: Researchers with a position at a Chinese institution; foreign researchers employed in China are eligible
grants.notes: Applications are normally submitted in Chinese — institutional support is essential.

grants.title: NSFC Young Scientists Fund (青年科学基金)
grants.funding_body: National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC)
grants.description: Entry-level NSFC grant for young researchers establishing an independent line of work in China.
grants.eligibility: Under age limits (typically 35 for men, 38 for women); position at a Chinese institution
grants.notes: Almost a rite of passage for junior faculty in China; age limits are strictly applied.

grants.title: NSFC Research Fund for International Scientists (RFIS)
grants.funding_body: National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC)
grants.description: NSFC grants specifically for non-Chinese scientists working at Chinese institutions, in young and senior tracks.
grants.eligibility: Non-Chinese nationals holding a position at a Chinese host institution
grants.notes: One of the few Chinese schemes designed around foreign researchers, with English application materials.

grants.title: CAS President's International Fellowship Initiative (PIFI)
grants.description: Brings international researchers to CAS institutes at every level, from PhD students and postdocs to visiting professors.
grants.amount: Monthly stipend by level (~¥8,000-20,000+) plus travel and insurance
grants.duration: Weeks to 2 years depending on category
grants.eligibility: Non-Chinese researchers with a CAS host institute; category-specific criteria
grants.application_mode: CAS PIFI online system via host institute
grants.notes: The most accessible entry into the Chinese research system; you need a CAS host to nominate you.

grants.title: China Postdoctoral Science Foundation Grants
grants.description: National postdoctoral funding in China, including general grants and special funding for outstanding candidates, plus international exchange programmes.
grants.eligibility: Postdocs registered in a Chinese postdoctoral station; some tracks open to international postdocs
grants.application_mode: CPSF online system via host station
grants.notes: The International Exchange Program also funds foreign postdocs coming to China.

grants.title: British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.description: The UK's premier early-career award in the humanities and social sciences, funding three years of independent research and a first monograph.
grants.amount: Full salary + up to ~£6,000/yr research expenses
grants.eligibility: PhD within ~3 years; UK host institution which must support the application
grants.notes: Host institutions run internal selection first — approach departments in the summer.

grants.title: ESRC Postdoctoral Fellowships & Doctoral Training
grants.description: The UK's main social science funder, supporting doctoral training partnerships and one-year postdoctoral fellowships to consolidate the PhD.
grants.amount: Doctoral: fees + ~£20k stipend; Postdoc: full salary + expenses
grants.eligibility: Doctoral via accredited DTPs; postdoctoral within ~1 year of PhD at a UK institution
grants.deadline_text: DTP deadlines ~Jan; postdoc via host institution (check site)
grants.notes: Applications go through accredited Doctoral Training Partnerships rather than directly to ESRC.

grants.title: SSHRC Doctoral & Postdoctoral Fellowships
grants.funding_body: Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)
grants.description: Canada's federal funder for the humanities and social sciences, with major doctoral and postdoctoral fellowship competitions.
grants.amount: Doctoral CAD 20-40k/yr; Postdoctoral CAD 45,000/yr + research allowance
grants.eligibility: Canadian citizens/permanent residents for most awards; postdoc requires PhD within eligibility window
grants.notes: University internal deadlines precede the SSHRC deadline by weeks — start early.

grants.title: ACLS Fellowships (American Council of Learned Societies)
grants.description: The leading US fellowship portfolio for the humanities, including dissertation completion, early-career and open competitions.
grants.eligibility: US-based scholars in the humanities and interpretive social sciences; specific rules per competition
grants.notes: The single most important non-federal humanities funder in the United States.

grants.title: SSRC International Dissertation Research Fellowship (IDRF)
grants.description: Funds doctoral students in the social sciences and humanities conducting dissertation fieldwork outside the United States.
grants.eligibility: Full-time PhD students at US universities, all but dissertation; fieldwork abroad
grants.notes: The standard fieldwork fellowship for US-based area studies and ethnographic research.

grants.title: Wenner-Gren Foundation Dissertation Fieldwork & Post-PhD Grants
grants.description: The world's leading dedicated funder of anthropological research, supporting fieldwork at doctoral and post-PhD level.
grants.amount: Dissertation up to $25,000; Post-PhD up to $25,000
grants.eligibility: Doctoral candidates and post-PhD researchers of any nationality, anywhere in the world
grants.notes: Genuinely international — no citizenship or host-country restriction.

grants.title: Gerda Henkel Foundation Research Scholarships
grants.description: German foundation funding research projects and scholarships across the historical humanities, open to international applicants.
grants.eligibility: Researchers in the historical humanities; any nationality; institutional affiliation expected
grants.notes: One of the few well-funded routes for archaeology, history and art history.

grants.title: Fritz Thyssen Foundation Grants & Fellowships
grants.description: German foundation supporting projects, conferences and fellowships, with a strong humanities and social science focus.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at German institutions or with a German connection; some international schemes
grants.deadline_text: Rolling submission with regular decision rounds
grants.notes: Rolling deadlines make it a good backup when the annual competitions have closed.

grants.title: Max Weber Programme for Postdoctoral Studies (EUI)
grants.category: Social sciences & humanities (economics, law, history, political science)
grants.description: Europe's largest postdoctoral programme in the social sciences, combining independent research with structured academic training in Florence.
grants.eligibility: PhD awarded within ~5 years; any nationality
grants.notes: Explicitly designed to prepare social scientists for the academic job market.

grants.title: JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan
grants.funding_body: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS)
grants.description: Short- and long-term fellowships inviting overseas researchers to collaborate with Japanese colleagues at host institutions.
grants.amount: Short-term: daily allowance + travel; Long-term: ~¥387,600/month + travel
grants.eligibility: Researchers based outside Japan with a PhD; nominated by the Japanese host researcher
grants.notes: Your Japanese host applies on your behalf, so start with the collaboration.

grants.title: Canon Foundation in Europe Research Fellowships
grants.description: Fellowships for European researchers to work in Japan (and Japanese researchers in Europe), across all fields.
grants.eligibility: Master's or PhD from a European institution (or Japanese equivalent); host arrangement required
grants.notes: One of the simplest routes for a European researcher to spend time in Japan.

grants.title: High-Tech Gründerfonds (HTGF)
grants.category: Seed investment (deep tech, life sciences, digital)
grants.description: Germany's most active seed investor, backed by the federal government and industry, typically the first institutional money into a spin-off.
grants.amount: €1M initial ticket, up to ~€4M+ in follow-on
grants.eligibility: German-registered high-tech startups, typically under 3 years old
grants.notes: Frequently pairs with EXIST: use the grant to reach a prototype, then raise from HTGF.

grants.title: INVEST — Grant for Venture Capital (Zuschuss für Wagniskapital)
grants.funding_body: German Federal Office for Economic Affairs (BAFA)
grants.description: Refunds 25% of an angel investor's stake in a young innovative German company, making it markedly easier to close a first round.
grants.amount: 25% of the investment refunded to the investor (up to €100k/yr per investor)
grants.eligibility: German innovative company under 7 years old, fewer than 50 employees; investor must apply too
grants.notes: Not money to you directly, but it materially improves your terms when negotiating with angels.

grants.title: Innosuisse Start-up Innovation Projects & Coaching
grants.description: Switzerland's federal innovation agency funds science-based innovation projects with research partners, plus structured start-up coaching and training.
grants.amount: Innovation projects: research partner costs covered (often CHF 100k-1M); coaching subsidised
grants.eligibility: Swiss-based company with a Swiss research partner; coaching open to early founders
grants.notes: Unusually, the money goes to your academic research partner — ideal for spin-offs still tied to a lab.

grants.title: Venture Kick
grants.description: Staged pre-seed funding for Swiss university spin-offs, awarded through three pitch rounds with escalating amounts.
grants.eligibility: Project based at a Swiss university or research institution; company may not yet exist
grants.interview: Yes — jury pitch at each stage
grants.notes: Staged design means a fast, low-risk first test of your idea. Very strong Swiss alumni record.

grants.title: Innovate UK Smart Grants
grants.description: The UK's main open innovation grant: funds game-changing, commercially viable R&D from any sector, with no set topics.
grants.eligibility: UK-registered business; can be single company or collaborative
grants.deadline_text: Regular rounds (~2-3 per year; check site)
grants.notes: 'Smart' means open to any technology — the flagship non-thematic UK grant.

grants.title: ICURe Programme (Innovation to Commercialisation of University Research)
grants.description: Pays university researchers to spend three months validating whether their research has a market, before committing to a spin-out.
grants.amount: ~£35,000 for market validation + follow-on grants up to £300k
grants.eligibility: Researchers at UK universities with commercialisable research; university must support
grants.notes: The UK's answer to NSF I-Corps: paid customer discovery before you commit.

grants.title: SEIS and EIS Investor Tax Relief
grants.description: UK tax schemes giving investors 50% (SEIS) or 30% (EIS) income tax relief, making it dramatically easier for early-stage companies to raise.
grants.amount: SEIS: up to £250k raised; EIS: up to £12M (£20M knowledge-intensive)
grants.eligibility: UK company meeting age, size and trade conditions; advance assurance recommended
grants.deadline_text: Rolling (apply for advance assurance before raising)
grants.notes: Knowledge-intensive companies (most deep tech) get extended limits and longer eligibility windows.

grants.title: Enterprise Ireland Pre-Seed Start Fund & HPSU Funding
grants.description: Ireland's state agency backs High Potential Start-Ups with equity and grants, plus a pre-seed fund for very early companies.
grants.eligibility: Irish-registered company with export potential; HPSU criteria apply
grants.notes: Also runs Commercialisation Fund grants for researchers pre-company.

grants.title: Enterprise Ireland Commercialisation Fund
grants.description: Funds researchers in Irish higher education and research institutes to develop innovations to the point of a licence or spin-out.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at Irish HEIs and research performing organisations
grants.notes: Ireland's equivalent of EXIST Research Transfer, run through the TTO.

grants.title: Vinnova Innovation Grants
grants.description: Sweden's innovation agency runs a wide range of calls, from small early-stage grants to large collaborative innovation programmes.
grants.eligibility: Swedish-registered organisations including startups; call-specific eligibility
grants.notes: Many calls are thematic; the 'Innovative Startups' track is the standard early-stage entry.

grants.title: Innovation Fund Denmark — Innobooster & InnoExplorer
grants.description: Denmark's innovation fund supports both researchers commercialising results (InnoExplorer) and companies developing products (Innobooster).
grants.amount: InnoExplorer up to DKK 1.5M; Innobooster typically DKK 0.5-5M
grants.eligibility: Danish companies, or researchers at Danish institutions for InnoExplorer
grants.notes: InnoExplorer is the pre-company route; Innobooster is for companies that already exist.

grants.title: Business Finland — Tempo & Research to Business (R2B)
grants.description: Finland's funding agency supports early startups (Tempo) and research groups preparing to commercialise or spin out (Research to Business).
grants.amount: Tempo up to €50k-100k; R2B up to €500k+
grants.eligibility: Finnish-registered startups (Tempo); Finnish research organisations (R2B)
grants.notes: R2B funds the research group directly — one of the most generous pre-company instruments in Europe.

grants.title: Innovation Norway — Market Clarification & Innovation Grants
grants.description: Norway's state agency funds startups through staged grants: market clarification, commercialisation, and scale-up support.
grants.eligibility: Norwegian-registered company with growth and international ambition
grants.notes: Staged structure means a small first grant is quite achievable and unlocks the larger ones.

grants.title: VLAIO Innovation Funding (Flanders)
grants.description: Flanders' agency funds development and research projects for companies, with dedicated instruments for young innovative firms.
grants.eligibility: Company with an operation in Flanders
grants.notes: Also runs innovation mandates that fund a researcher to prepare a spin-off.

grants.title: EIT Health Accelerator & Innovation Projects
grants.description: Europe's largest healthcare innovation network, running accelerator programmes, bootcamps and funded innovation projects for health startups.
grants.eligibility: Health/life-science startups and consortia in EU and associated countries
grants.notes: The most relevant EIT community for biomedical scientists founding companies.

grants.title: Industry Growth Program (Australia)
grants.funding_body: Australian Government — Department of Industry, Science and Resources
grants.description: Australia's flagship commercialisation programme: expert advice plus matched grants for innovative SMEs in national priority areas.
grants.amount: Early-stage commercialisation AUD 50k-250k; commercialisation/growth up to AUD 5M (matched)
grants.eligibility: Australian company with turnover under AUD 20M, working in a National Reconstruction Fund priority area
grants.notes: Replaced the earlier Accelerating Commercialisation programme; you must engage an Industry Partner adviser first.

grants.title: Australian R&D Tax Incentive
grants.description: Australia's largest innovation programme: a refundable tax offset that returns cash to loss-making startups conducting eligible R&D.
grants.amount: 43.5% refundable offset for companies under AUD 20M turnover
grants.eligibility: Australian company conducting eligible experimental R&D activities
grants.deadline_text: Annual registration within 10 months of financial year end
grants.notes: For a pre-revenue Australian startup this is often the single biggest source of cash.

grants.title: CSIRO Kick-Start
grants.funding_body: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO)
grants.description: Provides matched funding for Australian startups to access CSIRO's research expertise and facilities.
grants.eligibility: Australian company registered less than 3 years, or turnover under AUD 1.5M
grants.notes: Low-friction way to get national-lab-grade research into a young company.

grants.title: Main Sequence Ventures
grants.description: CSIRO-founded deep-tech venture fund investing in Australian science-based companies, often as first institutional money.
grants.eligibility: Australian deep-tech companies, frequently research spin-outs
grants.notes: Actively builds companies out of Australian research institutions, not just funds existing ones.

grants.title: Callaghan Innovation R&D Grants
grants.description: New Zealand's innovation agency funds business R&D through Ārohia Trailblazer grants, R&D experience grants and project co-funding.
grants.amount: Ārohia up to NZD 4M (matched); student/experience grants smaller
grants.eligibility: New Zealand-registered business conducting R&D in New Zealand
grants.notes: New Zealand also runs a 15% R&D Tax Incentive that most R&D-active startups should claim.

grants.title: New Zealand R&D Tax Incentive (RDTI)
grants.description: A 15% tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure, refundable in cash for loss-making companies within limits.
grants.amount: 15% credit on eligible R&D spend (min NZD 50k/yr)
grants.eligibility: New Zealand businesses performing eligible R&D
grants.deadline_text: Annual, tied to the tax year (check site)
grants.notes: The baseline support every R&D-active NZ startup should be using.

grants.title: NZ Growth Capital Partners — Aspire Fund
grants.description: New Zealand's government-backed early-stage investor, co-investing alongside angels in young New Zealand companies.
grants.eligibility: New Zealand-based startup with a lead private investor
grants.notes: Requires a private lead investor — this is matching capital, not first money.

grants.title: NEDO Entrepreneurs Programme (NEP) & Deep Tech Startup Support
grants.funding_body: New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO)
grants.description: Japan's main technology development agency funds deep-tech entrepreneurs from pre-company research through to large-scale development.
grants.amount: NEP up to ¥10M-40M; deep-tech programmes up to ¥2bn for later stages
grants.eligibility: Individuals or companies developing technology in Japan; programme-specific criteria
grants.notes: The Entrepreneurs Programme (NEP) supports individuals before a company exists — the natural first step.

grants.title: JST START (University Startup Support)
grants.description: Funds university researchers, together with a business promotion organisation, to develop research results toward a startup.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at Japanese universities with commercialisable results; business partner required
grants.notes: Japan's closest equivalent to EXIST or the Commercialisation Fund.

grants.title: J-Startup
grants.funding_body: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
grants.description: Government endorsement programme giving selected Japanese startups access to support, showcases and introductions rather than direct cash.
grants.amount: No direct grant — support, exposure and priority access
grants.eligibility: Selected Japanese startups; nomination by recommenders
grants.notes: Status rather than money, but it opens doors to Japanese corporates and other programmes.

grants.title: TIPS (Tech Incubator Program for Startups)
grants.funding_body: Korean Ministry of SMEs and Startups (MSS)
grants.description: Korea's flagship startup programme: a private accelerator invests, and the government matches with a much larger R&D grant.
grants.amount: Up to ₩500M R&D grant (plus ~₩100M+ private investment) — extensions to ₩1.5bn
grants.eligibility: Korean startup under 7 years old, selected and invested in by a TIPS operator
grants.notes: You cannot apply directly to the government — you must first be backed by an accredited TIPS operator.

grants.title: K-Startup Grand Challenge
grants.funding_body: National IT Industry Promotion Agency (NIPA), Korea
grants.description: Korea's flagship programme for foreign startups: a fully funded 3-month acceleration in Korea, with visas, stipend and follow-on funding for top teams.
grants.amount: ~KRW 20M+ settlement support during the programme; additional grants for winners
grants.eligibility: Non-Korean startups with at least one founder able to relocate to Korea
grants.notes: One of the few Asian programmes explicitly designed for foreign founders, including visa support.

grants.title: Korean Government Startup Support (K-Startup / KISED)
grants.funding_body: Korea Institute of Startup and Entrepreneurship Development (KISED)
grants.description: Umbrella for Korea's national startup programmes, including pre-startup packages, early-stage packages and scale-up support.
grants.amount: Pre-startup package up to ₩100M; early-stage packages up to ₩100M+
grants.eligibility: Korean-registered startups; some tracks open to foreign residents in Korea
grants.notes: Most application materials are in Korean; a Korean co-founder or partner makes this far more feasible.

grants.title: Startup SG Founder & Startup SG Tech
grants.category: Startup funding (all sectors, deep tech track)
grants.description: Singapore's national startup programme: mentorship plus capital for first-time founders, and proof-of-concept/value grants for deep tech.
grants.amount: Founder: up to SGD 50k (matched 3:1); Tech: POC up to SGD 250k, POV up to SGD 500k
grants.eligibility: Singapore-registered company, at least 30% local shareholding for several schemes
grants.deadline_text: Rolling via Accredited Mentor Partners / EnterpriseSG
grants.notes: Startup SG Tech is proof-of-concept money for genuinely deep technology — well suited to research spin-offs.

grants.title: SGInnovate Deep Tech Programmes
grants.description: Singapore government-owned deep-tech venture builder that invests in and supports science-based companies, plus talent programmes for researchers.
grants.amount: Investment tickets typically SGD 250k-2M; talent programmes vary
grants.eligibility: Deep-tech companies with a Singapore nexus; researchers for talent programmes
grants.notes: Also runs Summation and talent programmes that place researchers into deep-tech startups.

grants.title: HKSTP Incubation Programmes (Incu-Tech / Incu-Bio)
grants.funding_body: Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation (HKSTP)
grants.description: Hong Kong's flagship incubation programmes providing funding, subsidised lab and office space, and support for technology and biomedical startups.
grants.amount: Up to HKD 1.29M (Incu-Tech) / HKD 6M (Incu-Bio) in financial support
grants.eligibility: Startup incorporated in Hong Kong, typically under 5 years old
grants.notes: Incu-Bio includes access to shared wet-lab facilities — rare and expensive to replicate.

grants.title: Cyberport Incubation Programme
grants.description: Hong Kong's digital technology hub, offering funding, workspace and mentorship to early-stage digital and fintech startups.
grants.amount: Up to HKD 500k financial assistance (plus additional schemes)
grants.eligibility: Hong Kong-incorporated digital tech startup, typically under 3-5 years old
grants.notes: Focused on digital, fintech, AI and e-commerce rather than hardware or biotech.

grants.title: China Innovation Fund for Small Technology-Based Firms (Torch Programme)
grants.funding_body: Ministry of Science and Technology (MOST), China
grants.description: China's long-running national programme supporting small technology-based enterprises through grants, subsidies and incubator networks.
grants.eligibility: Chinese-registered small technology firms; provincial rules and quotas apply
grants.deadline_text: Provincial calls (varies; check local Science & Technology Bureau)
grants.notes: Administered provincially with substantial local variation — the local bureau is the real gatekeeper.

grants.title: DOD SBIR/STTR
grants.description: The largest SBIR programme by budget, funding US small businesses developing technologies with defence and dual-use applications.
grants.amount: Phase I ~$150-300k; Phase II ~$1-2M (Direct to Phase II available)
grants.duration: Phase I 6-12 months; Phase II 2 years
grants.eligibility: US small business, majority US-owned; topic-driven solicitations
grants.notes: Topic-driven: you must match a published need. Direct-to-Phase-II exists if you already have proof of concept.

grants.title: NASA SBIR/STTR
grants.description: Funds US small businesses developing technologies relevant to NASA's space, aeronautics and science missions.
grants.duration: Phase I 6 months; Phase II 24 months
grants.eligibility: US-based small business (<500 employees); STTR requires a research institution partner
grants.notes: Strong pathway if your technology has any space, sensing or materials angle.

grants.title: USDA SBIR
grants.description: Non-dilutive funding for US small businesses innovating in agriculture, food systems, forestry and rural development.
grants.amount: Phase I up to $175k; Phase II up to $650k
grants.duration: Phase I 8 months; Phase II 24 months
grants.eligibility: US small business; topic areas set annually
grants.notes: Much less crowded than NIH or NSF SBIR if your work touches agriculture or food.

grants.title: NSF Partnerships for Innovation (PFI)
grants.description: Helps academic teams translate NSF-funded research discoveries toward commercial products, including through new ventures.
grants.amount: Technology Translation up to $250k; Research Partnerships up to $550k
grants.eligibility: PI with prior NSF-funded research at a US institution
grants.notes: Requires a lineage to prior NSF funding — check the current solicitation for what qualifies.

grants.title: Breakthrough Energy Fellows
grants.description: Supports scientists and engineers turning climate technology research into companies, with funding, mentorship and a two-year programme.
grants.amount: Up to ~$500k+ in funding and support per project
grants.eligibility: Teams with a climate-relevant technology at an early stage; US, UK and EU cohorts
grants.notes: One of the strongest climate-tech routes for researchers who have not yet founded a company.

grants.title: Berliner Startup Stipendium
grants.description: Berlin's founder stipend: pays a salary to early founding teams while they develop their idea inside a partner incubator.
grants.eligibility: Founding teams based in Berlin, hosted by one of the partner incubators; company usually not yet founded
grants.deadline_text: Rolling intakes via partner incubators (check site)
grants.notes: One of the more accessible German Länder stipends; the incubator partner is your entry point.

grants.title: Gründerstipendium NRW
grants.funding_body: Ministry of Economic Affairs, North Rhine-Westphalia
grants.description: North Rhine-Westphalia's founder stipend, giving early founders a living allowance while validating a business idea.
grants.eligibility: Founders in NRW with an innovative idea; endorsement from an accredited start-up centre required
grants.application_mode: Via an accredited NRW start-up centre
grants.notes: Low-threshold and rolling — a practical first step for founders in Germany's most populous state.

grants.title: Start-up BW Pre-Seed
grants.funding_body: Baden-Württemberg Ministry of Economic Affairs / L-Bank
grants.description: Baden-Württemberg's pre-seed instrument, providing convertible-style public funding alongside a private co-investor.
grants.amount: Up to €800,000 public share (typically matched 80/20 with a co-investor)
grants.eligibility: Startup based in Baden-Württemberg with an accredited pre-seed partner as co-investor
grants.application_mode: Via a Start-up BW pre-seed partner
grants.notes: You approach an accredited partner (incubator or investor), not the state directly.

grants.title: BayStartUP & Bayerische Forschungsstiftung
grants.funding_body: Bavarian Ministry of Economic Affairs / BayStartUP
grants.description: Bavaria's startup network runs business plan competitions and investor matchmaking, while the Bavarian Research Foundation funds applied research projects including university-industry work.
grants.amount: Research foundation projects typically €100k-500k; competitions offer coaching and investor access
grants.eligibility: Bavarian companies and research institutions; competition entry open to founders in Bavaria
grants.notes: Bavaria also runs the m4 Award specifically for personalised-medicine startups.

grants.title: LOEWE Programme (Hesse)
grants.funding_body: State of Hesse — Ministry of Higher Education, Research and the Arts
grants.description: Hesse's flagship research programme funding excellence clusters, research groups and early-career projects at institutions in the state.
grants.amount: LOEWE Exploration ~€300k; clusters and centres far larger
grants.eligibility: Researchers at higher education and research institutions in Hesse
grants.notes: LOEWE Exploration funds unconventional, high-risk ideas with light-touch applications — a rare format.

grants.title: InnoRampUp & InnoFounder (Hamburg)
grants.description: Hamburg's two-tier startup support: InnoFounder pays a founder stipend with coaching, InnoRampUp grants fund technical development.
grants.eligibility: Startup located in (or relocating to) Hamburg
grants.notes: Also runs the Innovationsstarter Fonds Hamburg for equity investment.

grants.title: Technologiegründerstipendium & futureSAX (Saxony)
grants.funding_body: Saxon State Ministry for Economic Affairs / SAB
grants.description: Saxony's technology founder stipend supports researchers and graduates preparing a technology-based spin-off, alongside the futureSAX innovation platform.
grants.eligibility: Founders in Saxony with a technology-based idea, typically linked to a university or research institute
grants.notes: Dresden and Leipzig have strong microelectronics and biotech ecosystems behind this.

grants.title: Ikerbasque Research Fellowships & Professorships
grants.description: The Basque Country's science foundation recruits international researchers with five-year fellowships and permanent research professorships.
grants.amount: Fellowships: full salary + €25k research budget; Professorships permanent
grants.eligibility: PhD holders of any nationality; host institution in the Basque Country required
grants.notes: Fellowships can convert to a permanent position — unusually secure for a regional scheme.

grants.title: Beatriu de Pinós & FI Fellowships (Catalonia)
grants.funding_body: AGAUR — Agency for Management of University and Research Grants
grants.description: Catalonia's fellowship portfolio: FI grants fund doctoral candidates, Beatriu de Pinós brings experienced postdocs to Catalan institutions.
grants.duration: FI 3 years; Beatriu de Pinós 3 years
grants.eligibility: Beatriu de Pinós requires 2+ years abroad and a Catalan host; FI for doctoral candidates in Catalonia
grants.notes: Catalonia also runs ICREA for senior researchers — among the best-paid research positions in Spain.

grants.title: Atracción de Talento Investigador (Madrid)
grants.description: Madrid's talent attraction programme funds researchers to join universities and research centres in the region, in junior and senior modalities.
grants.eligibility: PhD holders; host institution in the Madrid region; modality-specific experience requirements
grants.application_mode: Comunidad de Madrid portal via host
grants.notes: Applications go through the host institution — line up your host well before the call opens.

grants.title: ACCIÓ Startup Capital (Catalonia)
grants.description: Catalonia's grant for technology-based startups in their first stages, covering product development and market entry.
grants.eligibility: Technology-based company registered in Catalonia, typically under 3 years old
grants.notes: Catalonia is Spain's densest startup ecosystem outside Madrid, with strong deep-tech support.

grants.title: Lazio Innova — Pre-seed & Innovation Grants
grants.description: The Rome region's development agency funds innovative startups and research-to-market projects through recurring regional calls.
grants.eligibility: Startups and SMEs based in the Lazio region
grants.notes: Italian regions vary enormously — Lombardy, Emilia-Romagna and Piedmont run parallel schemes.

grants.title: Innov'up & Paris Innovation Amorçage
grants.description: The Paris region's innovation funding, combining regional grants and repayable advances with incubator-linked seed funding.
grants.amount: Innov'up €30k-3M (grant + repayable advance); PIA up to €150k
grants.eligibility: Company based in Île-de-France; PIA requires an accredited Paris incubator
grants.notes: Paris Innovation Amorçage runs through incubators — join one first.

grants.title: Scottish EDGE & Scottish Enterprise High Growth Spin-out Programme
grants.description: Scotland's competition-based funding for early startups, alongside Scottish Enterprise's dedicated support for university spin-outs.
grants.amount: Scottish EDGE up to £150,000; HGSP grants for spin-out projects
grants.eligibility: Business based in Scotland; HGSP for academic spin-outs from Scottish institutions
grants.deadline_text: Scottish EDGE runs 2 rounds/yr; HGSP rolling
grants.notes: Scottish EDGE is pitch-competition style; HGSP is the route for university technology.

grants.title: Invest Northern Ireland Innovation Support
grants.description: Northern Ireland's economic development agency supports new and growing businesses with innovation grants, R&D funding and proof-of-concept support.
grants.amount: Proof of concept up to ~£50k; R&D grants larger
grants.eligibility: Business based in Northern Ireland
grants.notes: Northern Ireland companies can also access Republic of Ireland cross-border programmes.

grants.title: tech2b Incubator (Upper Austria)
grants.description: Upper Austria's academic incubator (part of the AplusB network) supporting technology founders with funding, coaching and infrastructure.
grants.eligibility: Founders based in (or relocating to) Upper Austria; technology or knowledge-based idea
grants.notes: Linz's strong mechatronics and software ecosystem sits behind this one.

grants.title: Standortagentur Tirol & aws Regional Programmes
grants.description: Tyrol's location agency funds innovation projects, cluster cooperation and startup support for companies in the region.
grants.eligibility: Company or founding team based in Tyrol
grants.notes: Innsbruck's life-science and sports-tech clusters are the regional strengths.

grants.title: Cancer Research UK Career Development Fellowship
grants.description: Europe's largest cancer charity funds researchers establishing their first independent cancer research group in the UK.
grants.eligibility: Postdocs ready for independence; UK host institution; any nationality
grants.notes: CRUK also funds PhD studentships, project awards and clinician scientist fellowships.

grants.title: British Heart Foundation Fellowships
grants.description: The UK's leading heart charity funds the full career ladder, from PhD studentships to intermediate and senior basic science fellowships.
grants.eligibility: Cardiovascular researchers at UK institutions
grants.notes: Basic Science and Clinical fellowship tracks run in parallel.

grants.title: American Cancer Society Research Grants & Fellowships
grants.description: The largest non-government US cancer funder, supporting postdoctoral fellowships and independent investigator research scholar grants.
grants.amount: Postdoc ~$66k/yr; Research Scholar Grants up to $825k over 4 years
grants.eligibility: US host institution; postdoc fellowships open to non-US citizens at US institutions
grants.notes: Postdoctoral fellowships are open to international researchers based in the US.

grants.title: Alzheimer's Association Research Grants
grants.description: The world's largest non-profit funder of Alzheimer's research, with fellowships, new-investigator grants and clinical trial support.
grants.amount: AARF fellowships ~$175k; AARG grants up to $150k/yr
grants.eligibility: Researchers worldwide — explicitly international; career-stage-specific tracks
grants.notes: Genuinely global funding — applicants from any country are eligible.

grants.title: Michael J. Fox Foundation Research Grants
grants.funding_body: Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research
grants.description: The largest non-profit funder of Parkinson's research, running targeted and open calls worldwide with an emphasis on translation.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at institutions worldwide; programme-specific criteria
grants.notes: Very fast, translation-focused review compared with government funders.

grants.title: Breakthrough T1D (formerly JDRF) Research Grants
grants.description: The leading global funder of type 1 diabetes research, funding postdoctoral fellowships, career development awards and research projects.
grants.eligibility: Researchers worldwide at eligible institutions
grants.notes: Renamed from JDRF in 2024 — older links and papers still use the JDRF name.

grants.title: Cystic Fibrosis Foundation Research Awards
grants.description: Funds the full pipeline of cystic fibrosis research, from postdoctoral fellowships to clinical trials, and is famous for venture philanthropy successes.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at eligible institutions; some awards international
grants.notes: The CFF's venture-philanthropy model helped produce the CF modulator drugs.

grants.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society Career Development Program
grants.description: Career development awards for researchers focused on leukemia, lymphoma and myeloma, from fellow to scholar level.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at institutions worldwide; career-stage tracks
grants.notes: International applicants are eligible — unusual for a US disease charity.

grants.title: MS Society & National MS Society Research Grants
grants.funding_body: UK MS Society / National Multiple Sclerosis Society (US)
grants.description: The two largest MS charities fund postdoctoral fellowships, project grants and clinical research on multiple sclerosis.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at eligible UK or US institutions respectively
grants.notes: Check both organisations — they fund complementary areas and have separate cycles.

grants.title: Parkinson's UK Research Grants
grants.description: The UK's leading Parkinson's charity funds studentships, fellowships and project grants, with strong patient involvement in review.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at UK institutions
grants.notes: People with Parkinson's sit on the review panels — write your lay summary carefully.

grants.title: Diabetes UK Research Grants
grants.description: Funds diabetes research across basic science, clinical studies and psychosocial research, including fellowships and studentships.
grants.amount: Project grants up to ~£500k; fellowships salary + costs
grants.eligibility: Researchers at UK institutions
grants.notes: Also funds a dedicated stream on the psychology of living with diabetes.

grants.title: Fondation pour la Recherche Médicale (FRM)
grants.description: France's largest private biomedical funder, supporting doctoral fourth-year funding, postdoctoral returns and team projects.
grants.eligibility: Researchers in French laboratories; nationality-open
grants.notes: The fourth-year doctoral funding is a lifeline where three-year contracts run out.

grants.title: AIRC Fellowships and Grants (Italy)
grants.funding_body: Fondazione AIRC per la Ricerca sul Cancro
grants.description: Italy's dominant cancer research funder, offering fellowships for Italy and abroad plus investigator and start-up grants.
grants.eligibility: Researchers in Italy; some fellowships fund Italians going abroad or returning
grants.notes: The Start-Up Grant is one of the best routes to independence for cancer researchers in Italy.

grants.title: Deutsche Krebshilfe (German Cancer Aid) Funding
grants.description: Germany's leading cancer charity funds research projects, priority programmes and the Mildred Scheel career development fellowships.
grants.amount: Project grants €200k-1M+; Mildred Scheel fellowships salary + costs
grants.eligibility: Researchers at German institutions; Mildred Scheel supports stays abroad
grants.notes: Mildred Scheel Early Career Centres also fund structured clinician-scientist programmes.

grants.title: Fondazione Telethon (Italy) — Genetic Disease Research
grants.description: Italy's dedicated funder for rare genetic disease research, from basic mechanisms through to gene therapy trials.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at Italian institutions (some international collaborations)
grants.notes: Behind several of the world's first approved gene therapies — strong translational track record.

grants.title: Worldwide Cancer Research Grants
grants.description: Funds early-stage discovery cancer research anywhere in the world, deliberately backing unconventional ideas.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at institutions in any country
grants.notes: Genuinely international with no host-country restriction — rare among cancer charities.

grants.title: MQ Mental Health Research Fellowships
grants.description: The UK's leading mental health research charity funds fellowships and projects across neuroscience, psychology and data science.
grants.eligibility: Early-career researchers; UK-based and some international eligibility
grants.notes: One of very few dedicated funders for mental health science outside government.

grants.title: Health Research Board (HRB) Ireland
grants.description: Ireland's national health research funder, with emerging investigator awards, applied partnership awards and PhD training programmes.
grants.amount: Emerging Investigator Awards up to ~€500k; other schemes vary
grants.eligibility: Researchers at Irish host institutions
grants.notes: Strong emphasis on patient and public involvement in the research design.

grants.title: Google PhD Fellowship Program
grants.description: Supports outstanding graduate students in computer science and related areas, pairing each fellow with a Google research mentor.
grants.amount: Full tuition and fees + stipend (regionally set, typically 2-3 years)
grants.eligibility: PhD students nominated by their university; regional programmes for Africa, Asia-Pacific, Europe, India, Latin America, North America
grants.notes: Universities may nominate only a limited number, so the internal deadline is the real one.

grants.title: Google Research Scholar Program
grants.description: Unrestricted gifts supporting early-career professors pursuing research in computing and related fields.
grants.eligibility: Faculty within ~7 years of their PhD at an eligible institution worldwide
grants.notes: Unrestricted funds are unusually flexible — no detailed budget justification required.

grants.title: Microsoft Research PhD Fellowship
grants.description: Two-year fellowships for exceptional PhD students in computing-related fields, with mentorship and an optional research internship.
grants.amount: Tuition and fees + stipend + conference allowance
grants.eligibility: PhD students at eligible universities; separate programmes for the Americas, EMEA and Asia
grants.application_mode: University nomination or direct (varies by region)
grants.notes: Microsoft also runs Accelerating Foundation Models Research with compute grants.

grants.title: Meta Research PhD Fellowship
grants.description: Supports promising doctoral students working in areas relevant to Meta's research, with two years of funding and community events.
grants.eligibility: PhD students worldwide in relevant fields; apply directly
grants.notes: Direct application, no university nomination needed — unlike Google's programme.

grants.title: NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship & Academic Grant Program
grants.description: Two tracks: fellowships for PhD students doing GPU-accelerated research, and hardware/compute grants for academic labs.
grants.amount: Fellowship up to $60,000; Academic grants provide GPUs or cloud compute
grants.eligibility: PhD students with completed research using GPU computing; academics for hardware grants
grants.notes: The hardware grant programme is much less competitive than the fellowship — worth knowing.

grants.title: IBM PhD Fellowship Program
grants.description: Supports doctoral students working in areas of mutual interest with IBM Research, including quantum computing and AI.
grants.eligibility: PhD students nominated by a faculty adviser at an eligible university worldwide
grants.notes: Requires faculty nomination and usually a research connection to IBM's areas.

grants.title: Amazon Research Awards
grants.description: Unrestricted awards plus AWS credits for academic researchers working in Amazon's areas of scientific interest.
grants.amount: Up to $80,000 cash + up to $40,000 AWS credits
grants.eligibility: Faculty at accredited universities worldwide; call-topic specific
grants.notes: The AWS credit component alone can be transformative for compute-heavy projects.

grants.title: Roche Postdoctoral Fellowship (RPF) Programme
grants.region: Switzerland, USA, Germany & other Roche sites
grants.description: Three-year postdoctoral positions run jointly between a Roche research site and an academic laboratory, on pre-competitive science.
grants.amount: Full Roche salary and benefits + research budget
grants.eligibility: PhD holders; project jointly proposed by a Roche scientist and an academic supervisor
grants.application_mode: Joint proposal via a Roche scientist
grants.notes: Publication is expected — this is genuinely academic-style research inside industry.

grants.title: Novartis FreeNovation & Novartis Foundation Grants
grants.description: FreeNovation funds unconventional, high-risk biomedical ideas from external researchers, with a deliberately light application process.
grants.eligibility: Academic researchers worldwide; open, unconstrained topics within life sciences
grants.notes: Deliberately short applications — designed to fund ideas that would fail conventional review.

grants.title: Bayer Foundation Fellowships (Jeff Schell & Otto Bayer)
grants.description: Fellowships supporting talented students and early researchers in life sciences, medicine, agriculture and sustainability, including research stays abroad.
grants.eligibility: Students and early-career researchers; specific fellowship tracks by field and career stage
grants.notes: Smaller amounts, but flexible funding for research stays that other schemes will not cover.

grants.title: Merck (Merck KGaA) Research Grants & Future Insight Prize
grants.description: Merck funds external research through open grant calls in areas such as drug discovery, sustainability and advanced materials.
grants.eligibility: Academic researchers worldwide; topics defined per call
grants.notes: Note this is Merck KGaA (Germany), distinct from Merck & Co (US, known as MSD outside North America).

grants.title: AstraZeneca Postdoctoral Research Programme
grants.region: UK, Sweden, USA & other AZ sites
grants.description: Industry postdoc positions with academic-style freedom, encouraging publication and often run jointly with a university partner.
grants.eligibility: PhD holders; positions advertised by research area and site
grants.notes: A genuine research career track — postdocs publish and present like academic peers.

grants.title: Pfizer Global Medical & Independent Grants (ASPIRE)
grants.description: Competitive grants for investigator-initiated clinical, health-outcomes and quality-improvement research in Pfizer's therapeutic areas.
grants.eligibility: Researchers and institutions worldwide; therapeutic-area specific calls
grants.notes: Review is deliberately independent of Pfizer's commercial teams; mainly relevant to clinical researchers.

grants.title: Johnson & Johnson WiSTEM2D Scholars Award
grants.category: Science, technology, engineering, maths, manufacturing & design
grants.description: Awards for women assistant professors advancing research across the STEM2D disciplines, with funding and mentorship.
grants.eligibility: Women in the first years of a tenure-track (or equivalent) position; global eligibility
grants.notes: Six disciplines, one award each per year — small numbers but genuinely global.

grants.title: Cloud & Compute Credits for Research (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure)
grants.funding_body: Amazon Web Services / Google Cloud / Microsoft Azure
grants.description: The major cloud providers all run research credit programmes giving academics free compute and storage for scientific projects.
grants.eligibility: Academic researchers and students; institution and project criteria vary by provider
grants.notes: Often overlooked but easy to obtain — credits can replace a large equipment budget line for computational work.

grants.title: Nobel Prize
grants.category: Physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, peace, economics
grants.description: The world's most prestigious award, recognising those who have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind across six categories.
grants.eligibility: By nomination only from qualified nominators (laureates, professors, academies)
grants.notes: You cannot nominate yourself; nominators are confidentially invited.
grants.category_clean: Life Sciences & Medicine;Natural Sciences & Engineering;Social Sciences & Humanities

grants.title: Breakthrough Prize
grants.description: The most lucrative science prize in the world, celebrating major achievements and funded by tech philanthropists.
grants.eligibility: Open nomination; anyone may nominate a candidate (not themselves)
grants.notes: Includes New Horizons prizes ($100k) for early-career physicists and mathematicians.

grants.title: Fields Medal
grants.description: Often called the 'Nobel of mathematics', awarded to up to four mathematicians under 40 at each International Congress.
grants.eligibility: Mathematicians under 40; by committee selection
grants.deadline_text: Awarded every 4 years at the ICM
grants.notes: The age limit makes it uniquely a young-researcher honour among top prizes.

grants.title: Wolf Prize
grants.category: Agriculture, chemistry, mathematics, medicine, physics & arts
grants.description: A prestigious Israeli award often seen as a predictor of the Nobel, recognising lifetime achievement across the sciences and arts.
grants.eligibility: By nomination; the foundation invites nominations from experts worldwide
grants.notes: Many Wolf laureates later receive the Nobel Prize.

grants.title: Kavli Prize
grants.funding_body: Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters / Kavli Foundation
grants.description: Recognises pioneering advances in three fields representing the largest, smallest and most complex systems in science.
grants.eligibility: By nomination from the international scientific community
grants.notes: Fills three fields the Nobel Prizes do not directly cover.

grants.title: Lasker Awards
grants.description: America's most respected biomedical research prize, frequently a precursor to the Nobel in Physiology or Medicine.
grants.eligibility: By nomination; nominations invited internationally
grants.notes: Known as 'America's Nobels' for their strong predictive record.

grants.title: Turing Award
grants.description: The highest distinction in computer science, recognising contributions of lasting technical importance to computing.
grants.eligibility: By nomination through the ACM awards process
grants.notes: Considered the 'Nobel Prize of computing'.

grants.title: Millennium Technology Prize
grants.description: One of the world's largest technology prizes, honouring innovations that improve quality of life and sustainable development.
grants.eligibility: By nomination; open to innovators whose technology is already in wide use
grants.notes: Rewards technologies already demonstrably benefiting society.

grants.title: EMBO Gold Medal
grants.description: Recognises outstanding contributions by young life scientists in Europe, typically within a decade of independence.
grants.eligibility: EMBO members and the community nominate; candidates usually under ~40
grants.notes: A leading marker of a rising European life scientist.

grants.title: EU Contest for Young Scientists (EUCYS)
grants.description: The EU's contest for 14-20 year old students, showcasing outstanding secondary-school research projects.
grants.eligibility: Students aged 14-20 selected via national competitions
grants.deadline_text: National rounds feed the EU final (check site)
grants.notes: Entry is through your country's national science competition.

grants.title: L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards
grants.description: Honours five eminent women scientists, one per world region, each year, alongside the separate rising-talent fellowships.
grants.eligibility: Women scientists of distinction; by nomination
grants.notes: The international awards are for established scientists; national programmes fund early-career women.

grants.title: Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists
grants.funding_body: Blavatnik Family Foundation & New York Academy of Sciences
grants.category: Life sciences, physical sciences & engineering, chemistry
grants.description: One of the world's largest unrestricted prizes for young scientists, with national and international streams.
grants.eligibility: Faculty under 42; nominated by their institution
grants.notes: Institution-nominated — your research office controls who goes forward.

grants.title: Vilcek Prizes
grants.description: Celebrates the contributions of immigrants to American science and culture, with prizes for established and rising researchers.
grants.eligibility: Foreign-born scientists working in the US; age limits for the Creative Promise awards
grants.notes: Unusually, you apply directly rather than being nominated.

grants.title: Eppendorf Award for Young European Investigators
grants.description: Recognises outstanding contributions to biomedical research in Europe by scientists under 35.
grants.eligibility: Researchers under 35 working in Europe; direct application
grants.notes: One of the few top European early-career prizes open to direct application.

grants.title: Science & SciLifeLab Prize for Young Scientists
grants.category: Molecular biology, cell biology, genomics, ecology & environment
grants.description: A global prize for recent PhD graduates, with the grand-prize essay published in Science.
grants.eligibility: PhD awarded within the past few years; essay-based entry
grants.notes: Essay competition — a strong writing sample matters as much as the science.

grants.title: Falling Walls Science Breakthroughs & Lab
grants.description: Falling Walls recognises annual science breakthroughs and runs the Falling Walls Lab pitch competition for young innovators.
grants.amount: Breakthrough recognition; Lab winners get prizes + Berlin finals
grants.eligibility: Researchers and innovators worldwide; Lab is for early-career pitchers
grants.deadline_text: Lab regional heats through the year; finals in November
grants.notes: The Falling Walls Lab is a 3-minute pitch format accessible to PhD students.

grants.title: EU Prize for Women Innovators
grants.description: Annual EU prize for the most talented women entrepreneurs behind innovative companies, with a Rising Innovators strand for younger founders.
grants.eligibility: Women founders/co-founders of a company registered in the EU or Associated Country
grants.notes: Prize money plus major visibility for fundraising.

grants.title: EIC Horizon Prizes
grants.description: Inducement prizes rewarding whoever best solves a defined societal challenge, from affordable batteries to early-warning systems.
grants.eligibility: Open to individuals, teams and companies meeting the challenge rules
grants.notes: You win by delivering a working solution, not by writing a proposal.

grants.title: MIT Technology Review Innovators Under 35
grants.description: A globally recognised annual list of 35 innovators under 35, with global and regional editions.
grants.eligibility: Innovators under 35; open nomination and self-nomination
grants.notes: Career-defining visibility; regional lists are a realistic entry point.

grants.title: Forbes 30 Under 30
grants.description: High-profile annual lists recognising young achievers across many categories including science and healthcare.
grants.eligibility: Under 30 in the relevant list year; nomination and self-nomination
grants.notes: The Science and Healthcare categories are the relevant ones for researchers.

grants.title: James Dyson Award
grants.description: International design and engineering award for students and recent graduates who invent something that solves a problem.
grants.eligibility: Current students or graduates within 4 years, in design/engineering fields
grants.notes: Prototype-driven — you submit a working invention, not just an idea.

grants.title: Young Inventors Prize (European Patent Office)
grants.description: EPO award celebrating inventors under 30 whose work contributes to the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
grants.amount: Cash prizes for top three (up to €20,000)
grants.eligibility: Inventors under 30 with an invention addressing the SDGs; by nomination
grants.notes: Focused on sustainability and real-world impact.

grants.title: Cartier Women's Initiative Award
grants.description: Global programme awarding grants and support to women entrepreneurs building businesses with strong social or environmental impact.
grants.eligibility: Women running an early-stage, for-profit, impact-driven business
grants.notes: Direct application — includes an executive education programme for fellows.

grants.title: Nordic Startup Awards & The Europas
grants.description: Ecosystem awards recognising Europe's most promising startups by category and region, offering visibility and investor exposure.
grants.eligibility: Startups in the relevant region and category; nomination and self-entry
grants.notes: Primarily visibility and networking rather than funding.

grants.title: Startup World Cup
