grants.description: A global pitch competition with regional rounds culminating in a grand final, offering a headline investment prize.
grants.eligibility: Startups competing through regional qualifying rounds worldwide
grants.deadline_text: Regional heats through the year (check site)
grants.notes: The grand prize is an investment, not a grant, but regional exposure is valuable.

grants.title: National Medal of Science
grants.funding_body: US National Science Foundation / White House
grants.description: The highest US honour for scientists and engineers, awarded by the President for outstanding lifetime contributions.
grants.eligibility: US citizens; by nomination through the NSF process
grants.notes: The most prestigious science honour conferred by the US government.

grants.title: NAS Awards (National Academy of Sciences)
grants.description: A portfolio of prestigious disciplinary awards spanning chemistry, physics, biology, mathematics and the social sciences.
grants.eligibility: By nomination; open to researchers internationally for several awards
grants.notes: Includes the NAS Award in Molecular Biology, often an early-Nobel signal.

grants.title: Alan T. Waterman Award
grants.description: The US government's highest honour for early-career scientists and engineers.
grants.eligibility: US citizens/permanent residents under 40 or within 10 years of PhD; by nomination
grants.notes: One of the few top honours reserved specifically for young researchers.

grants.title: MacArthur Fellowship ('Genius Grant')
grants.funding_body: John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation
grants.description: The famous 'no-strings' fellowship for extraordinarily creative individuals, awarded across sciences, arts and humanities.
grants.eligibility: US residents/citizens; by confidential nomination only — no applications
grants.notes: You cannot apply or know you were nominated; recipients are surprised by a phone call.

grants.title: Shaw Prize
grants.category: Astronomy, life science & medicine, mathematical sciences
grants.description: A major international award, sometimes called the 'Nobel of the East', for recent breakthroughs in three fields.
grants.eligibility: By nomination from the international community
grants.notes: Based in Hong Kong; among the most lucrative science prizes globally.

grants.title: Gairdner Awards
grants.description: Canada's premier biomedical research prize, with a strong record of preceding the Nobel.
grants.eligibility: By nomination; international candidates eligible
grants.notes: Roughly a quarter of Gairdner laureates go on to win a Nobel.

grants.title: Killam Prizes & Killam Fellowships
grants.funding_body: National Research Council of Canada (Killam Program)
grants.category: Natural sciences, health sciences, engineering, social sciences & humanities
grants.description: Among Canada's most distinguished awards for scholars, recognising career achievement and funding two years of research freedom.
grants.amount: Prizes CAD 100,000; Fellowships up to CAD 160,000
grants.eligibility: Canadian scholars; by nomination
grants.notes: The Killam Fellowships buy out two years of teaching for full-time research.
grants.category_clean: Life Sciences & Medicine;Natural Sciences & Engineering;Social Sciences & Humanities

grants.title: NSERC Prizes (Herzberg, Steacie, Polanyi)
grants.funding_body: Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC)
grants.description: NSERC's suite of national honours, including the Herzberg Gold Medal (top prize) and the Steacie Memorial Fellowships for young researchers.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at Canadian institutions; by nomination
grants.notes: The Steacie Fellowships are the key early-to-mid-career honour.

grants.title: Banting Award / CIHR Prizes
grants.description: CIHR's recognition awards celebrating outstanding health research achievements across Canada.
grants.eligibility: Health researchers in Canada; by nomination
grants.notes: Named partly for Frederick Banting, co-discoverer of insulin.

grants.title: Royal Society Medals & Awards (Copley, Davy, Darwin)
grants.description: The Royal Society's medals include the Copley Medal, the world's oldest scientific prize, plus premier awards across the sciences.
grants.eligibility: By nomination; several medals open to international candidates
grants.notes: The Copley Medal dates to 1731 and predates the Nobel by 170 years.

grants.title: Royal Society Research Merit / early-career medals
grants.description: Includes early-career medals such as the Francis Crick Medal for a scientist in the early stage of their career.
grants.eligibility: UK-based researchers for several; by nomination
grants.notes: The Francis Crick Medal specifically targets early-career biologists.

grants.title: Royal Academy of Engineering — MacRobert Award
grants.description: The UK's premier prize for engineering innovation, awarded for a demonstrable commercial or social benefit.
grants.eligibility: UK-based engineering teams and companies; by entry/nomination
grants.notes: Focused on engineering that has reached real-world impact.

grants.title: Academy of Medical Sciences — Awards & Medals
grants.description: Recognises excellence in medical research, including career awards and the prestigious medals of the Academy.
grants.eligibility: UK-based biomedical researchers; by nomination
grants.notes: Also runs career development grants alongside its honours.

grants.title: Royal Irish Academy Gold Medals
grants.description: Ireland's highest academic accolade, recognising outstanding scholarly contributions across the sciences and humanities.
grants.eligibility: Scholars connected to Ireland; by nomination
grants.notes: Ireland's premier learned-society honour.

grants.title: Descartes Prize / EU research recognition
grants.description: EU-level recognition for outstanding collaborative research achievements by transnational teams (successor recognitions continue under Horizon Europe).
grants.eligibility: Transnational research collaborations in EU/associated countries
grants.notes: Celebrates the collaborative, cross-border nature of European research.

grants.title: Körber European Science Prize
grants.description: One of Europe's most valuable science prizes, funding a specific forward-looking research project by a leading European scientist.
grants.eligibility: Researchers working in Europe; by nomination
grants.notes: The money funds future research rather than rewarding past work alone.

grants.title: Balzan Prize
grants.description: A major prize across rotating fields in the sciences and humanities, requiring half the award to fund young researchers.
grants.eligibility: By nomination; fields rotate each year
grants.notes: Uniquely, laureates must devote half the prize to funding young scholars.

grants.title: Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine
grants.description: A leading European biomedical prize, funding ongoing research by scientists working in Council of Europe member states.
grants.eligibility: Researchers in Council of Europe states; by nomination
grants.notes: Most of the prize is earmarked to continue the laureate's research.

grants.title: Brain Prize (Lundbeck Foundation)
grants.description: The world's largest neuroscience prize, recognising outstanding contributions to brain research.
grants.eligibility: By nomination; open internationally
grants.notes: The single most prestigious award in neuroscience.

grants.title: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize
grants.description: Germany's most important research prize, giving laureates exceptional funding freedom for their ongoing work.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at German institutions; by nomination
grants.notes: The best-funded research prize in the world by award amount.

grants.title: Leopoldina & Max Planck Research Awards
grants.description: German national-academy and Max Planck honours recognising internationally outstanding researchers, several open to non-German scientists.
grants.eligibility: By nomination; several open internationally
grants.notes: The Max Planck Research Award explicitly funds international collaboration.

grants.title: CNRS Gold, Silver & Bronze Medals
grants.funding_body: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS)
grants.description: France's national research honours: the Gold Medal for lifetime achievement, Silver for established and Bronze for early-career researchers.
grants.eligibility: Researchers connected to French science; by nomination
grants.notes: The Bronze Medal is a notable early-career marker in France.

grants.title: Spinoza & Stevin Prizes (NWO)
grants.description: The Netherlands' highest scientific awards — the Spinoza Prize for scientific excellence and the Stevin Prize for societal impact.
grants.eligibility: Researchers at Dutch institutions; by nomination
grants.notes: Often called the 'Dutch Nobel'; the money funds future research.

grants.title: Marcus Wallenberg & Crafoord Prizes
grants.funding_body: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences / Wallenberg
grants.category: Fields not covered by the Nobel (Crafoord); forestry (Wallenberg)
grants.description: Swedish international prizes filling gaps left by the Nobel — the Crafoord Prize covers mathematics, geosciences, biosciences and astronomy.
grants.eligibility: By nomination; international candidates
grants.notes: The Crafoord deliberately covers sciences the Nobel omits.

grants.title: Novozymes Prize & Novo Nordisk Prize
grants.description: Major Danish international prizes recognising outstanding biomedical and biotechnology research.
grants.eligibility: By nomination; open internationally
grants.notes: Among the largest life-science prizes in the Nordic region.

grants.title: ERC-style national young academy memberships / Die Junge Akademie
grants.description: Membership-based recognition for outstanding early-career researchers, offering funding, networks and a national platform.
grants.eligibility: Outstanding researchers 3-7 years post-PhD; by application/nomination
grants.notes: Most European countries now have an equivalent 'young academy'.

grants.title: For Women in Science National Rising Talent Awards
grants.description: National rising-talent fellowships (distinct from the international awards) supporting early-career women scientists in dozens of countries.
grants.eligibility: Women PhD students and postdocs; nationality/residency per country programme
grants.notes: Runs in over 100 countries — check your national programme's specifics.

grants.title: ASPIRE / national academies' early-career medals
grants.description: Most national science academies award early-career medals (e.g. the Australian Academy's Fenner and Gottschalk awards, the Royal Society of Canada's medals).
grants.eligibility: Early-career researchers in the relevant country; by nomination
grants.notes: Check your national academy — nearly all run early- and mid-career honorific awards.

grants.title: Wihuri, Sofja Kovalevskaja & other 'bring-a-star' awards
grants.funding_body: Various (Humboldt Sofja Kovalevskaja, Wihuri Foundation, etc.)
grants.description: Prize-style awards that fund a talented young researcher to build a group in a new country — half prize, half start-up grant.
grants.eligibility: Outstanding researchers (usually <6 yrs post-PhD) relocating; scheme-specific
grants.notes: The Sofja Kovalevskaja Award is one of the most generous young-researcher prizes in the world.

grants.title: National Inventors / Innovation Awards (EPO European Inventor Award)
grants.description: The EPO's flagship award celebrating inventors whose patented work has delivered major technical and societal impact.
grants.eligibility: Inventors with granted European patents; by nomination
grants.notes: Categories include Industry, Research, SMEs and a Popular Prize public vote.

grants.title: US Presidential / national startup & SBIR Tibbetts Awards
grants.description: The Tibbetts Award recognises SBIR/STTR-funded small businesses that exemplify excellence in high-tech innovation.
grants.eligibility: US small businesses with a strong SBIR/STTR record; by nomination
grants.notes: National recognition that strengthens future funding and investor credibility.

grants.title: Canada — Manning Innovation Awards
grants.description: Canada's principal awards celebrating Canadian innovators who have commercialised new products and technologies.
grants.eligibility: Canadian innovators with a marketed innovation; by nomination
grants.notes: Recognises commercialised innovation specifically, not just invention.

grants.title: EU Social Innovation Competition
grants.description: An annual challenge-based competition rewarding the best early-stage social innovations addressing a defined yearly theme.
grants.eligibility: Individuals and organisations in EU/associated countries; by application
grants.notes: Theme changes each year; strong route for impact-driven founders.

grants.title: James Dyson Award — national stages
grants.description: National rounds of the Dyson Award across ~30 countries, feeding the international final — a realistic entry point for student inventors.
grants.eligibility: Students/recent graduates in participating countries
grants.notes: Winning even the national stage is a strong signal for early hardware founders.

grants.title: Regional deep-tech prizes (Hello Tomorrow Global Challenge)
grants.description: A global deep-tech competition connecting early science-based startups with investors and industry, with sizeable cash prizes.
grants.eligibility: Early-stage deep-tech startups worldwide; by application
grants.notes: Specifically built for science-based ventures — a strong fit for research spin-offs.
